A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TimeXL research. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison, and the equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification experiments on four datasets, component ablations, explanation analyses and Finance regression experiments in Appendix F.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results, including regression experiments in Appendix G, and adds encoder sensitivity results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The prototype encoders, objectives, projection, prediction fusion, three LLM agents and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The regression adaptation is retained. Appendix C discusses prospective cost-saving strategies without documenting a revision to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Weather, Finance and the two Healthcare datasets for the same classification tasks, plus Finance regression. The new sensitivity analyses reuse existing coverage. Describing Finance as extended from its source does not establish a between-version dataset extension.

E2.justification: The same 18 baselines participate in the classification and regression comparisons, including MM-iTransformer, MM-PatchTST and TimeCAP. The GPT-4o-mini and Gemini-2.0-Flash backbone comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: The added sensitivity analyses specify single-kernel prototype-length sweeps on Weather and Finance using refined test texts. These are additional evaluation procedures; the original 6:2:2 splits, metrics, backbone choices and hyperparameter-search ranges remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds regularization-strength and prototype-length sensitivity analyses, and Appendix C adds computational-cost analysis. Existing ablations and case studies remain, with revised Finance explanation examples. V2 Figure 26's numerical/trend prediction visualization is removed.

E5.justification: V3 Tables 4–6 introduce mean-plus/minus reporting for the sensitivity results, whereas v2 reports no such uncertainty values. Both versions state five experimental runs; no increase is documented, and v3 does not define whether the ± quantities are standard deviations, standard errors or another statistic.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, backbone and regression scores are unchanged. V3 adds sensitivity results, such as Finance F1 of 0.430 versus 0.588 at time-prototype lengths 1 versus 5, and runtime estimates. Finance prototype examples are revised, and v2 Figure 26's prediction traces are removed.

T1.justification: The problem definition, similarity and fusion equations, regularization objectives and prototype projection mathematics are retained. Neither version adds distinct theorems, proofs or formal assumptions relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same prototype-and-LLM framework claims, four-dataset scope and up-to-8.9% AUC improvement claim. The additional analyses support existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations connecting regularization and prototype length to meaningful representations, and discusses computational practicality. It removes v2's explicit limitation that broader regression, long-term forecasting and forecasting under domain shifts remain unexplored.

D1.justification: New Appendix C documents workload, token usage and serial/parallel latency assumptions. Conversely, Appendix A.1 drops S&P Global Commodity Insights as the Finance news provider, and Finance figures replace specific index identifiers with generic feature labels. Existing prompts, hardware and hyperparameter information remain.

R1.justification: V3 prunes supporting citations, including ReAct, UniTime, GPT4MTS and Kolodner's case-based reasoning overview. It retains the same three related-work areas and essentially the same positioning of TimeXL's contribution.

P1.justification: V3 adds TimeXL to the title, updates affiliations and venue text, lightly edits prose and generalizes Finance terminology. Appendix B is expanded, a cost appendix is inserted, and the closing limitations and broader-impact sections are removed; the main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: The full ablation table moves from v2 Appendix Table 4 into main-text Table 2, replacing the F1-only display. V3 adds three sensitivity tables, expands Figure 3 with previously shown Weather examples, updates Finance figures and removes v2 Figure 26. Most other figures are retained with layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity studies and explicit cost assumptions make robustness and computational practicality easier to assess. These are modest gains, partly offset by less specific Finance provenance and feature labels, removal of the long-horizon/domain-shift limitation, and undefined ± statistics. The central method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
